cards.title: Chain of Command
cards.instruction: Treat every question, favor, and decision as something that must travel through the proper hierarchy.

cards.title: Start the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Get someone else to explain, announce, or begin the emotionally difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As eldest, you should tell Mum we're selling the house.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're the one who wants to sell it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The proposal originated below you. The announcement requires seniority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't hide behind my birthday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm respecting the family hierarchy. You say 'selling'; I'll explain the plumbing afterwards.

before.seedUse: The choir cancellation and house sale are Drive seeds; delegating the announcement up the authority chain embodies the Stance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're the eldest. You tell Mum I think it's time to sell her house.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're twins. You're forty seconds younger. Tell her yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll submit the proposal to you, and you can raise it with Mum.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I reject the proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She'll want to know what you've rejected. Could you start with that?

after.seedUse: Retains the house-sale and delegated first word from D101-single-b, and procedural routing from S67-single-b. Twins and the forty-second seniority gap are new illustrative details. B exercises the authority A invoked; A uses the rejection as another reason for B to begin.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 use seniority to delegate the announcement, so both cards are present. A5 explains the family hierarchy again.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 challenges ownership; A3 answers through rank. B4 names the birthday excuse, but A5 mostly repeats it rather than using that challenge.

relationship.evidence: B resists but cannot materially change the task. The older sibling only objects twice.

heightening.evidence: A5 divides selling from plumbing, a useful small variation, but the rank-based excuse survives unchanged.

specificity.evidence: A1 clearly establishes siblings, their mother and a proposed house sale.

brevityWit.evidence: The plumbing detail is usable; originated below you and respecting the family hierarchy explain more than the scene needs.

records.recommendedEdit: Let B reject the proposal as the senior sibling. A must then turn that actual rejection into the opening of the difficult conversation, rather than repeat the rank rule.
records.remainingConcern: The siblings' authority is A's comic interpretation, not a claim about real authority to sell a parent's house.

cards.title: Practical Realist
cards.instruction: Accept any unusual premise without debate. Focus immediately on schedules, costs, safety, and what must happen next.

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine, the ceiling predicts floods. Before discussing who broke the pipe, what's its maintenance budget?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you break the pipe?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First we need somewhere dry for its microphone. Prophecy carries poorly over running water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're avoiding the question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm prioritising electrics. Who insured a talking ceiling against its own predictions?

before.seedUse: The talking ceiling and dragon retain unusual-premise acceptance; logistical questions explicitly divert from the damage or expense A is avoiding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office ceiling says it saw who set off the sprinklers. Have we budgeted for a witness microphone?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't need one. It says you did it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need a transcript. Nobody should take notes under live sprinklers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's writing your name in the damp on the wall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we read it, let's get a quote for repainting.

after.seedUse: Uses the talking ceiling and microphone from S22-single-a, and the redirection away from damage in D14-single-a. Sprinklers and a written accusation are new details in the same office incident; each logistical intervention diverts the inquiry.

cardFidelity.evidence: A accepts the talking ceiling and diverts blame through logistics, but predicts floods and broken-pipe causation compete with that simple fusion.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 introduces a microphone after the maintenance-budget opening. B4 names avoidance rather than changing the evidence or logistical obstacle.

relationship.evidence: B has a credible interest in who broke the pipe, yet B4 only diagnoses A instead of making a new offer.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds insurance, another practical topic, without exploiting a concrete new development from B4.

specificity.evidence: Office flooding is usable; a predictive ceiling that requires a microphone adds setup not supported by the other lines.

brevityWit.evidence: Prophecy carries poorly over running water is a detachable aside. The ending explains another diversion rather than sharpening the first.

records.recommendedEdit: Keep one impossible witness and one avoided accusation. Have B solve A's transcription excuse by putting the name on the wall, giving A a practical reason to repaint the evidence.
records.remainingConcern: The writing ceiling is an illustrative extension of the speaking-building premise. Do not import extra supernatural rules into the real scene.
records.reviewer: Assistant internal editorial review; no professional accreditation or independent human test claimed

cards.title: Practical Realist
cards.instruction: Accept any unusual premise without debate. Focus immediately on schedules, costs, safety, and what must happen next.

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dragon can inspect the rent letter later. Which meter covers its fire?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says you spent the rent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the dragon's gas contribution is suddenly very relevant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: On curtains, apparently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Flame-resistant curtains? We should check that before opening another financial question.

before.seedUse: The talking ceiling and dragon retain unusual-premise acceptance; logistical questions explicitly divert from the damage or expense A is avoiding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dragon can move in. Before we open that rent letter, who's paying for its fire insurance?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you use our rent to buy it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's establish whether we insure it as a pet or a boiler.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I called the insurer. They just want the receipt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll price fireproof filing cabinets. The paperwork clearly isn't safe here.

after.seedUse: Preserves the dragon sharing a flat from S22-single-b and the unopened rent letter from D14-single-b. Dragon purchase, insurance and a receipt are new links replacing the unrelated curtains. A redirects from purchase accountability to a sequence of practical requirements.

cardFidelity.evidence: Gas accounting plus avoiding a letter suggests both cards, but the dragon is oddly asked to inspect the letter instead of functioning as a logistical problem.

responseLogic.evidence: The rent, curtains, dragon and gas meter are individually comprehensible. The sequence jumps between four objects without one stable practical diversion.

relationship.evidence: B supplies financial facts but does not affect how A must pursue the diversion beyond naming curtains.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds flame resistance, though B4 merely identifies a purchase rather than presenting a new safety constraint.

specificity.evidence: A shared flat, pet and rent are playable. The dragon reading financial paperwork is an unnecessary premise.

brevityWit.evidence: Suddenly very relevant and opening another financial question are explanatory connective phrases rather than natural speech.

records.recommendedEdit: Tie the rent avoidance to insuring a newly acquired dragon. B obtains the insurance answer; the requested receipt then forces A to switch to fireproof storage rather than answering about the purchase.
records.remainingConcern: The final line is deliberately a flimsy practical excuse. It should be played sincerely, not as an instruction that B accept the diversion.
records.reviewer: Assistant internal editorial review; no professional accreditation or independent human test claimed

cards.title: Cleared to Know
cards.instruction: Treat access to private information as proof that you belong, and exclusion from any detail as a challenge to your legitimacy.

cards.title: How Much Do You Know?
cards.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the insider account of the party. Did the cake make it as far as the balcony?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do you know about the balcony?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I belong on the full briefing list. I'm checking how full it is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We hadn't mentioned a balcony.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then don't exclude me from the bit you haven't established yet.

before.seedUse: A uses insider entitlement to probe exactly how much is known, while B's questions threaten to expose A's suspiciously precise knowledge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm family. Why am I getting the public version of what happened to the wedding cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone dropped it off the balcony.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does the family version include a name?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you tell me where you were.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You want my alibi before giving me family gossip? That's the police version.

after.seedUse: Uses the family/public-summary distinction from S124-single-a and the cake/balcony probe from D06-single-a. A wedding replaces the separate reunion and party as one shared setting. Unlike the original, B supplies the balcony and A withholds an alibi.

cardFidelity.evidence: A requests insider access, but immediately supplies the balcony detail. That weakens the Drive to probe while disclosing very little.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 and B4 both react to the leaked detail. A5 asks for a bit not established yet, which does not follow the factual information B supplies.

relationship.evidence: B credibly suspects A, but the second challenge repeats the first rather than imposing a new condition.

heightening.evidence: The final demand adds no more precise probe or stakes; it merely repeats the demand for inclusion.

specificity.evidence: A party, cake and balcony establish enough concrete context.

brevityWit.evidence: Checking how full a full briefing is repeats wording without a substantial comic escalation.

records.recommendedEdit: Do not have A volunteer the secret detail. Let B disclose the balcony, make A ask for a name, and have B request an alibi. A can reject the transaction as an insult to family membership without answering.
records.remainingConcern: A need not actually be guilty. The illustration establishes guarded interest and a refusal to disclose, not an unseen crime solution.
records.reviewer: Assistant internal editorial review; no professional accreditation or independent human test claimed

cards.title: Cleared to Know
cards.instruction: Treat access to private information as proof that you belong, and exclusion from any detail as a challenge to your legitimacy.

cards.title: How Much Do You Know?
cards.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does the committee's private report mention a drain beside the missing keys?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What drain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stacked every chair. I deserve more than the public summary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're supplying details, not requesting them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then perhaps I should help decide which details remain confidential.

before.seedUse: A uses insider entitlement to probe exactly how much is known, while B's questions threaten to expose A's suspiciously precise knowledge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why is my report on the missing keys censored? I'm on this committee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's for the inner committee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can an outer member at least know where they were found?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The location starts with 'under'. That's all you get.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What would I have to chair to earn the next word?

after.seedUse: Retains the committee report and exclusion from S124-single-b and the missing-key inquiry from D06-single-b. A no longer leaks the drain. A proposed chair role converts belonging into a route to increasingly specific information.

cardFidelity.evidence: A volunteers the drain in A1 and changes to controlling confidentiality in A5. That drifts from probing while revealing little.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 challenges the new drain detail; A3 switches to chair-stacking membership rather than answering the challenge. B4 accurately notices the leak.

relationship.evidence: B challenges A meaningfully, but A neither changes the question nor makes the new membership claim consequential.

heightening.evidence: A5 seeks an editorial role over the report, a new goal instead of heightened information-seeking.

specificity.evidence: Committee, keys and report provide a clear context; the chair history is introduced only as an excuse.

brevityWit.evidence: The scene explains its own information leak and ends with a broad confidentiality suggestion rather than a precise new probe.

records.recommendedEdit: Use redaction as the membership insult and withhold new details from A. B offers only the first word of the location; A bargains for a committee office to earn the next word.
records.remainingConcern: A’s private stake stays unstated. The Drive is expressed by guarded extraction, and the chair proposal should sound like a serious membership bid rather than an unrelated pun.
records.reviewer: Assistant internal editorial review; no professional accreditation or independent human test claimed

cards.title: Everything Is Policy
cards.instruction: Treat every personal choice as evidence of a larger system. Connect exceptions, habits, and coincidences until they become institutional doctrine.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always make tea after we argue. Shall we finish the reconciliation procedure before your taxi?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made the tea. We're done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tea initiates the procedure. Agreement closes it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What agreement?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That you want tomorrow's tea with me too. Then I can authorise the taxi.

before.seedUse: The Stance turns ordinary recurring personal choices into policy; A uses this policy specifically to delay departure until repair is explicit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always make tea after we argue. We can't close the reconciliation meeting with two full cups.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pour mine away. My taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're disposing of unfinished business. That has to go in the minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll drink it in the taxi.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So we're moving the reconciliation meeting. I'll get my coat.

after.seedUse: Uses post-argument tea classified as policy from S192-single-b and the taxi-after-conflict scene in D74-single-b as a compatible setting. The stored seedRefs preserve the exact indexed source association; the broader seed family is acknowledged here. A redefines disposal and transport as reconciliation decisions.

cardFidelity.evidence: Tea becomes a formal reconciliation procedure and A seeks confirmation of future contact. Both cards work.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 reinterprets B2's tea completion. B4 only asks for clarification, so A5 supplies a condition rather than responding to resistance.

relationship.evidence: B needs to leave, but the final B question gives A an easy opening instead of challenging the emotional procedural trap.

heightening.evidence: Tomorrow’s tea is a warmer stake; the final authorization repeats the rule-first tactic rather than transforming it.

specificity.evidence: Post-argument tea and an arriving taxi are concrete and compact.

brevityWit.evidence: The final tomorrow-tea phrase is promising. Agreement closes it and authorise the taxi are slightly over-explanatory together.

records.recommendedEdit: Give B two concrete exit tactics: discard the tea, then take it along. A turns each personal choice into a new institutional interpretation and follows the meeting rather than just adding another form.
records.remainingConcern: A’s decision to fetch a coat is an offer to continue contact, not a guarantee that B or the driver admits A. The relationship is still unresolved.
records.reviewer: Assistant internal editorial review; no professional accreditation or independent human test claimed

cards.title: Everything Is Policy
cards.instruction: Treat every personal choice as evidence of a larger system. Connect exceptions, habits, and coincidences until they become institutional doctrine.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You usually say 'see you tomorrow' before leaving. Is its absence a policy change?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just tired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We'll record fatigue as an exception, not permanent withdrawal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I go now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After confirming the exception still includes seeing me tomorrow.

before.seedUse: The Stance turns ordinary recurring personal choices into policy; A uses this policy specifically to delay departure until repair is explicit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always say 'see you tomorrow' before leaving. Does tonight's silence mean our argument changed the policy?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It means I'm tired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then please say it. I need to know we're still on speaking terms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: See you next Tuesday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a suspension, not a goodbye. Can we hold the appeal before your taxi gets here?

after.seedUse: Uses ordinary behavior elevated to policy from S192-single-a/b and postponing departure until emotional repair from D74-single-b. The repeated goodbye is retained from the prior pair version; the postponed date is new pressure supplied by B.

cardFidelity.evidence: A treats omitted routine words as a policy change and delays departure for reassurance, matching the pair.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 supplies tiredness and A3 labels it an exception. B4 asks to leave; A5 reasserts the original confirmation request.

relationship.evidence: B has a credible fatigue motive but B4 introduces no new constraint beyond the already stated departure.

heightening.evidence: A5 repeats tomorrow under the label exception instead of developing the institutional reading when tested.

specificity.evidence: The everyday goodbye ritual provides recognizable, sufficiently specific relationship context.

brevityWit.evidence: Permanent withdrawal is witty but formal. The unchanged final request is longer than its comic contribution.

records.recommendedEdit: Let B actually offer a later goodbye, not just request permission to leave. A should treat the delayed next contact as suspension and ask for an immediate appeal, making B4 necessary to the ending.
records.remainingConcern: Next Tuesday is deliberately an unspecified later date; the dialogue makes no unsupported claim about how many days away it is. B’s line can be exhausted rather than cruel.
records.reviewer: Assistant internal editorial review; no professional accreditation or independent human test claimed

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've taken charge of the broken-vase investigation. Questions require my approval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is there glue on your hand?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approved question. I'll appoint myself lead investigator of the glue.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a piece of vase stuck to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent work. You're promoted to observing other people while I preserve this evidence.

before.seedUse: A turns the exact culprit investigation into a status performance, claiming the authority to assess incriminating evidence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've opened an inquiry into the broken vase. I'll be chairing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good question. You're authorised to inspect the glue cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No. I want to inspect you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent initiative. I'll supervise. Start with my clean hand.

after.seedUse: Retains the vase and glue investigation from D13-single-a, and the gracious approval of initiative from S01-single-a. The clean-hand restriction is a new response to B’s explicit inspection demand; A uses authority to narrow evidence while appearing helpful.

cardFidelity.evidence: A chairs the inquiry and redirects incriminating clues. A1 states Questions require my approval rather than demonstrating that assumption.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers the glue question with investigation. B4 adds more attached evidence; A5 diverts B to other people without changing the method.

relationship.evidence: B brings physical evidence but is simply reassigned away from it in the final line.

heightening.evidence: Promotion to observing other people is a twist, yet it avoids the stronger challenge of B demanding to examine A directly.

specificity.evidence: Broken vase, glue and attached shard form one playable incident.

brevityWit.evidence: The explicit questions/approval rule and long promotion announcement make the joke sound like a card explanation.

records.recommendedEdit: Remove the spoken explanation of the approval rule. B should reject the cupboard assignment and demand to examine A. Have A graciously permit that inspection while specifying only the clean hand.
records.remainingConcern: A’s evasiveness is obvious to the audience by design. The card requires attempted concealment, not a successful deception.
records.reviewer: Assistant internal editorial review; no professional accreditation or independent human test claimed

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've authorised an inquiry into the dead office plant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll investigate the coffee machine under my supervision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made the coffee too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Useful connection. I'll decide how much weight to give your promising theory.

before.seedUse: A turns the exact culprit investigation into a status performance, claiming the authority to assess incriminating evidence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've authorised a full inquiry into who gave the office fern espresso.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did. I'm your manager, and I watched you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. An eyewitness. I'll need a written account of when you noticed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: While you were pouring it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we have a witness who could have intervened. Thank you for coming forward.

after.seedUse: Preserves the dead office plant and coffee from D13-single-b, and ignoring actual ownership/status in S01-single-b. Manager/eyewitness status is new. A neither denies the evidence nor yields rank; A redirects blame by classifying B’s observation as a missed intervention.

cardFidelity.evidence: A acts as inquiry leader while being blamed, but says little to hide responsibility beyond questioning the coffee machine.

responseLogic.evidence: B adds responsibility for making the coffee; A5 dismisses its weight. The new detail does not force a concrete altered tactic.

relationship.evidence: B supplies evidence twice; A gets to judge both contributions without B exercising independent leverage.

heightening.evidence: A5 repeats control of evidence rather than making the fact that A brewed the coffee change the investigation.

specificity.evidence: The dead office plant and coffee provide an immediately understandable problem.

brevityWit.evidence: Promising theory and decide how much weight are abstract evaluations rather than a sharp performed reversal.

records.recommendedEdit: Give B real status and eyewitness evidence. A must keep treating that manager as a subordinate witness and turn the reported time of observation into an omission by B, appearing to advance the inquiry.
records.remainingConcern: The scene demonstrates A’s self-serving investigative reframing, not a claim that the manager actually caused the harm.
